title: The automatic pass is latched per state counter, which the owner ruling of 2026-08-29 (“THE CLIENT MAY NOT HOLD A…”)(b) rules out
summary: The owner ruling of 2026-08-29 (“THE CLIENT MAY NOT HOLD A…”)(b) rules that an automatic answer (it names the haste-step ready and the automatic pass) is latched by being unanswered, never by a state counter, because states keep arriving while an intent is outstanding. The owner ruling of 2026-08-29 (“the affordances that must stay live…”) says the automatic pass is latched once per actionCount via takeAutoPass, and test 70 [59] asserts that a new state number re-opens the latch. If a state with a new actionCount reaches a seat while its automatic pass is still outstanding, a second pass could go out and come back refused. The verifier confirmed it in the client: the haste ready was converted (hasteAutoOut), but the automatic pass still goes through takeAutoPass, keyed on actionCount.

title: The live action counter tells the opponent when you act inside every hidden simultaneous segment
summary: A hidden simultaneous segment is meant to show nobody the other side's plays until everyone is done (owner ruling of 2026-08-18, “Haste step engine model […]”). The owner ruling of 2026-08-28 (“the haste step readies itself, and…”) measured that GameState.actionCount is served live to both seats and rises on every action, so a modified client sees when its opponent acts in the resource step, the haste step and deployment. The shipped client renders nothing from it.
